challengeDetails.title: Commercializing Low Earth Orbit (LEO)

projectDetails.summary: Astro Sweepers is a compliance‑and‑insight platform that automates NASA’s Debris Assessment Software (DAS) workflow, generates ODAR/EOMP reports and produces clear, actionable risk scores for space operators. It uses our proprietary ASRI index to weight debris legacy, compliance readiness, collision‑risk burden and sustainability alignment, combining NASA SPARK/Space‑Track data and DAS outputs to produce before and after risk scores and long‑term debris population forecasts. The system includes a user‑friendly web portal that transforms technical analyses into intuitive dashboards and business‑ready reports, helping customers reduce post‑mission lifetimes, lower casualty risks and demonstrate regulatory compliance to insurers, investors and agencies. Ultimately, Astro Sweepers aims to mitigate the mounting orbital‑debris crisis by tying immediate DAS compliance with longer‑term sustainability forecasting and a scalable business model, enabling safer, more sustainable access to low Earth orbit.

challengeDetails.title: Animation Celebration of Terra Data!

projectDetails.summary:
Project A.T.L.A.S. is an immersive web experience guided by NASA's Terra satellite, personified as a friendly 3D storyteller.

The journey begins with an interactive tour of the satellite itself, where Terra introduces its five "senses"—the instruments that make its stories possible (MODIS, MOPITT, ASTER, MISR, and CERES).

From there, the experience dives into two powerful, interconnected memories: the 2004 Amazon fires (“A Forest’s Fever”) and the catastrophic 2024 Southern Brazil floods (“A Deluge of Tears”).

Our story uses layered data to reveal a profound insight: how a wound to the planet in the past contributed to a tragedy in the present.

After the guided tour, the controls are handed over. In a free-explore mode, users can scrub through 25 years of Terra data, layer instruments, and make their own discoveries.

A.T.L.A.S. is designed to reduce data friction for educators, communicators, and citizens, turning NASA's vast archives into clear, actionable stories. We turn seeing into understanding, and understanding into action.

challengeDetails.title: Sharks from Space

projectDetails.summary:
Our project develops a predictive foraging habitat web application for endangered whale sharks (𝘙𝘩𝘪𝘯𝘤𝘰𝘥𝘰𝘯 𝘵𝘺𝘱𝘶𝘴) in Philippine waters, the heart of the Coral Triangle—home to unparalleled marine biodiversity that supports local livelihoods. Whale sharks face growing threats from ship strikes, tourism pressure, and climate change, making conservation planning urgent.

Using Google Earth Engine, we built a MaxEnt-based model that integrates NASA satellite data (sea surface temperature, chlorophyll-a, ocean currents, and bathymetry) with 48 verified sightings to forecast monthly whale shark foraging habitats from 2025–2030. The system achieves robust accuracy (AUC > 0.87), providing a reliable framework for identifying seasonal hotspots and supporting marine protected area management.

To advance monitoring, we propose next-generation bio-telemetry tags that pair environmental sensors with molecular prey detection, transmitting real-time data via satellite for continuous model refinement.

This work delivers a scalable, data-driven solution for whale shark conservation by combining machine learning, remote sensing, and proposes an innovative tagging technology. Beyond safeguarding this iconic species, the project establishes baseline data for climate change impact assessments, strengthens ecotourism sustainability, and contributes to global marine biodiversity protection efforts.

challengeDetails.title: Will It Rain On My Parade?

projectDetails.summary:
The Weather Risk Assistant is a web application designed to provide a detailed historical weather analysis for any location and date worldwide. By leveraging over 30 years of daily data from the NASA POWER Project, our tool directly addresses the challenge of making complex Earth observation data accessible and actionable for long-term planning.

The application allows users to input a location and a future date to receive a personalized dashboard showing the historical probability of extreme conditions like 'Very Hot', 'Very Wet', or 'Very Uncomfortable'. It also displays historical averages and long-term climate trends through intuitive charts and a plain-English summary.

This is important because it empowers individuals, event planners, and travelers to make informed decisions months in advance, far beyond the scope of standard weather forecasts. By revealing localized climate trends for specific dates, it also makes the impacts of our changing environment personal and understandable.

challengeDetails.title: Will It Rain On My Parade?

projectDetails.summary:
Weatherly is a next-generation long-term weather prediction platform that combines advanced machine learning models with NASA POWER’s historical weather data to deliver accurate forecasts according to a user’s submitted location and date.
Unlike standard traditional weather apps that simply show temperature and rainfall, Weatherly goes further. It provides a complete activity suitability analysis, enabling users to know in advance whether the chosen day is ideal for their planned event. Whether it’s a cricket match, festival, parade, or outdoor celebration, "Weatherly" predicts not just the weather, but how it will affect the comfort and safety of your plans.
Weatherly is designed to make long-term weather analysis stable, reliable, and globally accessible. It empowers users worldwide to plan with confidence, by giving them both precise predictions and clear comfort-level recommendations for their activities.

Key Features of "Weatherly" includes
- Event-specific forecasts that predict weather for a specific location, date, and event type
- Event suitability that shows predicted weather as high, medium, or low risk levels
- Weather descriptions such as very rainy, sunny, cloudy, snowy, or windy
- Detailed metrics that provide temperature, rain probability, and wind speed data
- Long-term forecasts that can predict weather up to one year in advance
- Clear climate condition charts of 7 day forecasts
- A responsive design
- A system powered entirely by open NASA datasets

It emphasizes the importance of scientific awareness, critical thinking and curiosity about our solar environment. Ultimately, Oops! challengeDetails.title: A World Away: Hunting for Exoplanets with AI

projectDetails.summary: We developed a convolutional neural network (CNN) model capable of processing previously cleaned datasets. It receives parameters through a platform and, considering the light curves of the candidates, determines whether or not they classify as exoplanets. The model was trained using a standard 80/10/10 data split, training, evaluation, and testing respectively, optimized with binary cross-entropy loss in order to increase our accuracy, thus achieving 96.38% accuracy. challengeDetails.title: SpaceTrash Hack: Revolutionizing Recycling on Mars

projectDetails.summary:
Our project tackles three critical challenges for Martian colonization: the hazardous buildup of polymeric waste, the danger of cosmic radiation, and the immense cost of transporting materials from Earth. Our solution is a revolutionary process that transforms this waste into a lightweight, high-quality, and protective insulator. 
The strategic advantage is turning a liability into an asset. 

A closed-loop system is created where a dangerous liability (trash) is transformed into a vital asset (shielding and building materials). We propose a ‘biological factory’, where each component plays a vital role. Bacteria act as our biological recyclers, breaking down the tough polymeric waste into a raw, workable base. We then mix in Martian regolith for structural strength and a small amount of a bio-resin, which creates a smooth, homogenous 'ink' ready for molding. After this, mycelium fungi, the living binder, is introduced as fungal spores that grow a dense root network throughout the ink, weaving all the components together into a solid composite. Finally, the planet's intense UV radiation cures the bio-resin, hardening the entire structure into a durable and protective building block.

challengeDetails.title: Commercializing Low Earth Orbit (LEO)

projectDetails.summary:
We developed Gaia-LEO, a mixed-integer optimization framework that co-designs orbital and terrestrial data-center networks for the next generation of AI and Earth-observation workloads. The model jointly optimizes facility location, network topology, and workload placement by minimizing total CapEx + OpEx while satisfying real-world physical constraints latency, bandwidth, power, and thermal limits. Each orbital module represents a 40 MW containerized data-center node with solar power and radiative cooling; ground sites anchor fiber backhaul and user access. Using inputs from NASA’s CO2 emissions, water & orbital debris data and web scraped data center data the solver decides which orbital clusters to launch, which ground points of presence to activate, and how to route traffic through optical & inter-satellite links.

This framework directly addresses the challenge of commercializing LEO by quantifying when and where orbital compute becomes economically advantageous compared with terrestrial infrastructure. It transforms space from a communications relay into a computational layer – a sustainable, solar-powered extension of Earth’s cloud. The result is an actionable blueprint for scaling AI training and climate modeling in orbit, reducing terrestrial power and water footprints, and accelerating humanity’s transition toward space-based green compute as part of the emerging orbital economy.

challengeDetails.title: A World Away: Hunting for Exoplanets with AI

projectDetails.summary: This project presents an interactive web interface that applies ensemble-based machine learning to NASA’s publicly available datasets for exoplanet identification. Noticing the rapid pace of space technology, future missions will generate richer and more diverse datasets, making adaptable models essential. To address this, we designed multiple mission-specific models, with Kepler and TESS serving as initial examples. Our approach shows how machine learning can classify objects of interest more quickly and reliably than manual methods, while remaining flexible enough to integrate new data as it becomes available. The models employ a stacking ensemble of XGBoost, LightGBM, and CatBoost to maximize accuracy and robustness. Beyond accuracy, we emphasized feature engineering and a reliable pipeline to ensure methodological integrity and lasting innovation. While tailored to individual missions, the framework can also extend to other datasets with the required features, offering broader applicability. The frontend, built with Astro, React, Three.js, and Tailwind, enables users to upload and analyze datasets, retrain models, and view real-time results. On the backend, FastAPI service validates inputs, preprocesses data, and delivers predictions via APIs. Looking ahead, we aim to expand with high-performance models for future missions. Our slogan, “Continents apart, worlds away together,” reflects the global collaboration that drives this project.

challengeDetails.title: Build a Space Biology Knowledge Engine

projectDetails.summary:
We are a passionate team of engineers, data scientists, and physicists who believe that the key to our future in space lies in decoding the secrets of life itself.
At MEMORA LAB, we have joined forces to create an intelligent platform that transforms NASA’s vast archive of space biology research into an interactive experience of knowledge and discovery.

Our project, enables users to explore biological experiments conducted in space, understand how living organisms adapt to microgravity, and visualize how these discoveries connect across decades of missions.
Using artificial intelligence, knowledge graphs, and statistical analysis, our system organizes and connects hundreds of scientific papers — revealing relationships not only between experiments, organisms, and biological outcomes, but also among the scientists and research teams behind them.

Users can explore how life adapts to space environments, visualize collaborations, and identify emerging trends through interactive graphs and data-driven summaries.

challengeDetails.title: Commercializing Low Earth Orbit (LEO)

projectDetails.summary:
OrbitalHive is a self-sustaining orbital platform that integrates autonomous debris extraction, in-situ resource utilization, and In-Space Biomanufacturing (ISBM) to create the first circular economy in Low Earth Orbit (LEO).
Equipped with dual robotic extraction arms and a Tag-and-Tow tether system, OrbitalHive captures and stabilizes both structured and irregular debris. Using in-situ scanning technologies like Laser-Induced Breakdown Spectroscopy (LIBS) and X-Ray Fluorescence (XRF), it identifies material composition before recycling. Recovered metals are purified and fed into an additive manufacturing unit, where advanced 3D printers produce replacement components, satellite modules, and repair tools directly in orbit—reducing launch costs and dependency on Earth.
The In-Space Biomanufacturing Module (ISBM), located in the lower layer, harnesses the microgravity environment for pharmaceutical synthesis, protein crystallization, and biomaterial production. These processes yield higher molecular precision, enabling the development of next-generation therapeutics and materials impossible to achieve on Earth.
By combining AI-driven autonomy, tether-assisted debris retrieval, and bio-industrial synergy, OrbitalHive redefines sustainable space operations—turning orbital waste into industrial feedstock and transforming space into a productive ecosystem for both technology and life sciences.

Our goal is to deliver useful, scalable, and reproducible technology for cleaner skies, combining cloud computing, real data, and future improvements such as broader regions, longer prediction horizons, and integration of advanced deep-learning models. challengeDetails.title: A World Away: Hunting for Exoplanets with AI

projectDetails.summary:
Resonant Worlds Explorer is an AI-powered system that ingests telescope and satellite data, including spectra from missions like JWST, to search for exoplanets and detect possible biosignatures. Unlike traditional tools that rely on approximate floating-point methods, our system integrates Modulus, a new exact-math solver that converts physics and chemistry problems into number theory and solves them without numerical error. This allows us to model planetary atmospheres with high precision, test chemical equilibrium, and distinguish true biosignatures (like O₂ + CH₄ coexistence) from abiotic false positives.
We built a full end-to-end pipeline: fetching NASA data, detecting exoplanets with transit algorithms, validating signals with physics models, and running Modulus-based chemistry checks. Results are presented in a web interface with visual plots and automatically generated scientific reports.
This matters because the search for life beyond Earth depends on accuracy. By combining astronomy data, physics validation, and exact chemistry, Resonant Worlds Explorer reduces false positives and provides a reliable way to identify promising candidates for habitability, helping guide future missions and discoveries.

projectDetails.summary:
AEXIS is an AI-powered platform designed to automate the identification and classification of exoplanets using NASA’s open datasets from Kepler, K2, and TESS missions. 
It applies machine learning and deep learning models to analyze stellar light curves and other parameters, significantly reducing manual workload while improving the accuracy of exoplanet detection. 
AEXIS provides an intuitive web interface that allows both researchers and space enthusiasts to explore NASA’s exoplanetary data, visualize model predictions, and contribute to scientific discovery. 
The system bridges the gap between AI technology and astronomical research, fostering faster insights and new discoveries in space exploration.

challengeDetails.title: Data Pathways to Healthy Cities and Human Settlements

projectDetails.summary:
Our project is a web-based platform that unites global public databases with real-time community input to provide a comprehensive view of environmental and social challenges. Using AI, it analyses and condenses complex datasets into clear, neutral, and accessible insights, ensuring that users—from policymakers to planners to the general public—can quickly grasp key issues and trends.

The platform offers detailed information on air and water pollution, water risks, natural disasters such as droughts, floods, and wildfires, as well as heat stress and population density. Forecasting models extend this further, enabling proactive planning and risk anticipation to support more resilient human settlements.

Community engagement adds depth: through feedback and safety-reporting tools, citizens can highlight local issues, such as poorly lit or unsafe areas. This ground-level knowledge complements large-scale data, creating a more complete and accurate picture.

By merging advanced analytics with community-driven insights, the platform fosters collaboration between citizens and authorities, drives evidence-based decision-making, and helps shape safer, more inclusive, and sustainable cities. In essence, it transforms data into action, bridging global systems and local realities to support better urban planning and more responsive governance.

challengeDetails.title: Deep Dive: Immersive Data Stories from Ocean to Sky

projectDetails.summary:
Team Titan presents “Blue Point: The Legacy of the Ocean”, an immersive Virtual Reality (VR) experience that transforms raw NASA ocean data into a captivating visual and sound narrative.

Our project addresses the challenge “Deep Dive: Immersive Data Stories from Ocean to Sky” by placing the user in the role of a space explorer whose spacecraft encounters Earth as a potential new home. Through an interactive analysis system, the VR experience takes the user on a journey from space to the ocean depths, highlighting the complex relationship between oceans.

challengeDetails.title: Will It Rain On My Parade?

projectDetails.summary:
SkySense is a web-app platform that uses NASA Earth observation data and AI analysis to provide ultra-local and personalized weather predictions. Our goal is to help users plan outdoor events, sports, and travel with greater accuracy and confidence. By integrating NASA, Google, and Gemini APIs, SkySense analyzes multiple weather variables such as rain, wind, temperature, humidity, and visibility to generate real-time risk assessments and suggest the safest time windows for activities. 
The platform also features TwisterBot, a smart conversational assistant that delivers adaptive alerts, reminders, and weather insights directly to the user.
SkySense addresses the challenge of unreliable, generic forecasts by making meteorological data understandable and actionable. It would empower individuals and organizations to make informed decisions, reduce weather-related risks, and transform uncertainty into confidence.

challengeDetails.title: Embiggen Your Eyes!

projectDetails.summary: Cosmo Scope is an immersive, browser-based 3D solar system explorer that transforms real NASA datasets into a gamified learning experience. Users can seamlessly navigate planets, dive into interactive 2D maps, and use a timeline slider to travel through history and observe planetary changes. Built with cutting-edge web technologies, CosmoScope combines authentic space data, smooth 3D/2D transitions, and engaging missions where players act as time-traveling astronauts investigating mysterious signals from Earth. By blending education with interactive storytelling, CosmoScope makes the wonders of space exploration accessible, engaging, and inspiring for learners and enthusiasts of all ages.

challengeDetails.title: NASA Farm Navigators: Using NASA Data Exploration in Agriculture

projectDetails.summary:
Welcome to Henry’s Farm Adventure!
For the NASA Farm Navigators Challenge, we didn’t just build a game, we built a global farming quest powered by space data.

Meet Henry, a struggling farmer whose crops keep failing. Instead of giving up, he sets off on an epic journey around the world, guided by real NASA satellite data. Along the way, he meets farmers on the frontlines of climate change, like Bilal in Pakistan, fighting the floods of 2022, and Ramesh in India, surviving brutal heatwaves.

But this isn’t just a story, it’s you in action. As the player, you step into Henry’s boots and take on mini-games that transform serious challenges into hands-on missions, by solving them, you learn how farmers adapt in real life, how NASA’s data reveals these risks, and how communities can fight back against climate change.

This is NASA data like you’ve never seen it before, not in charts or reports, but in the palm of your hand, as a playful, high-stakes adventure.
